a1.he: גְּמָ׳ תַּנְיָא: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״לְבַת״ לְרַבּוֹת אוֹר שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד.

a2.he: רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ קַמֵּיהּ דְּבַר קַפָּרָא, שַׁבְקֵיהּ וַאֲתָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא. יוֹמָא חַד פְּגַע בֵּיהּ, בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ: זָב שֶׁרָאָה שָׁלֹשׁ רְאִיּוֹת בְּלֵיל שְׁמִינִי, מָה בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים בְּדָבָר זֶה?

a3.he: טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּבֵית הִלֵּל בְּמַפֶּלֶת בַּלַּיְלָה מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב: ״לְבַת״, אֲבָל זָב שֶׁרָאָה שָׁלֹשׁ רְאִיּוֹת בְּלֵיל שְׁמִינִי – פָּטְרִי, דְּלָא מְיַיתְּרִי קְרָאֵי, אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא שְׁנָא?

a4.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר קַפָּרָא: מָה בָּבְלִי אוֹמֵר בְּדָבָר זֶה? אִישְׁתִּיק רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא, לָא אֲמַר כְּלוּם. אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר קַפָּרָא: צְרִיכִין לְדִבְרֵי עִיָּיא? נַחְזוֹר עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״לְבַת״ – לְרַבּוֹת אוֹר שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד.

a5.he: נֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי: זָב שֶׁרָאָה שָׁלֹשׁ רְאִיּוֹת בְּלֵיל שְׁמִינִי, תָּנֵי חֲדָא: מֵבִיא, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא. מַאי לַָאו תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּהָא דְּתַנְיָא מֵבִיא, קָסָבַר: לַיְלָה אֵין מְחוּסַּר זְמַן, וְהָדְתָנֵי אֵין מֵבִיא, קָסָבַר: לַיְלָה מְחוּסַּר זְמַן?

a6.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי סָבְרִי לַיְלָה מְחוּסַּר זְמַן. וְהָא דְּתַנְיָא מֵבִיא – בְּזָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת, וְהָדְתַנְיָא אֵין מֵבִיא – בְּזָב בַּעַל שָׁלֹשׁ רְאִיּוֹת.

a7.he: זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא? הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: דַּוְקָא רָאָה בְּלֵיל שְׁמִינִי, אֲבָל בִּימָמָא דִּשְׁבִיעִי, לָא. קָסָבַר: כׇּל רְאִיָּיה שֶׁסּוֹתֶרֶת – אֵין מְבִיאָה לִידֵי קׇרְבָּן.

a8.he: אָמַר רָבָא: אַמַּאי אוֹקֵימְתַּאּ לְהָא דְּתַנְיָא אֵין מֵבִיא – בְּזָב בַּעַל שָׁלֹשׁ רְאִיּוֹת, לִיתְנְיַיהּ גַּבֵּי, חֲמִשָּׁה מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל עֲבֵירוֹת הַרְבֵּה! – לָא פְּסִיקָא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רָאָה אַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה וּשְׁתַּיִם בַּיּוֹם – מֵבִיא, שְׁתַּיִם בַּלַּיְלָה וְאַחַת בַּיּוֹם – אֵין מֵבִיא.

a9.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: תֵּדַע דְּאַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה וּשְׁתַּיִם בַּיּוֹם מֵבִיא, דְּהָא רְאִיָּיה רִאשׁוֹנָה שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע בְּעָלְמָא, וְאִילּוּ חָזֵי תַּרְתֵּין אַחְרָנְיָיתָא מִצְטָרְפִי לְהוּ.

a10.he: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? רְאִיָּיה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל זָב – חַזְיַיהּ בִּזְמַן חִיּוּבָא. אַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה, כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו בִּזְמַן חִיּוּבָא חַזְיַיהּ, אִי לָאו דְּאַשְׁמְעִינַן רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּמִצְטַרְפָא, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לָא תִּצְטְרֵף.

a11.he: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לַיְלָה מְחוּסַּר זְמַן?

a12.he: וְהָאָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: נִטְמָא בַּיּוֹם – מֵבִיא, בַּלַּיְלָה – אֵין מֵבִיא. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בַּלַּיְלָה – מֵבִיא!

a13.he: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: ״שְׁתַּיִם בַּלַּיְלָה וְאַחַת בַּיּוֹם – אֵין מֵבִיא״, לְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר מְחוּסַּר זְמַן.

a14.he: לְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר? פְּשִׁיטָא! רָאָה אַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה וּשְׁתַּיִם בַּיּוֹם אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ. מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו בִּזְמַן חִיּוּבָא קָחָזֵי לֵיהּ – לָא תִּצְטְרֵף, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a15.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ סְפֵק חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וּסְפֵק חָמֵשׁ זִיבוֹת – מְבִיאָה קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד וְאוֹכֶלֶת בִּזְבָחִים וְאֵין הַשְּׁאָר עָלֶיהָ חוֹבָה. חָמֵשׁ זִיבוֹת וַדָּאוֹת וְחָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדָּאוֹת – מְבִיאָה קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד וְאוֹכֶלֶת בִּזְבָחִים וְהַשְּׁאָר עָלֶיהָ חוֹבָה.

a16.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָמְדוּ קִינִּין בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם בְּדִינַר זָהָב, אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: הַמָּעוֹן הַזֶּה, לֹא אָלִין הַלַּיְלָה עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּדִינָרִין (בַּסּוֹף) [כֶּסֶף!] נִכְנַס לְבֵית דִּין וְלִמֵּד: ״הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדָּאוֹת חָמֵשׁ זִיבוֹת וַדָּאוֹת – מְבִיאָה קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד וְאוֹכֶלֶת בִּזְבָחִים וְאֵין הַשְּׁאָר עָלֶיהָ חוֹבָה״ וְעָמְדוּ קִינִּין בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא בְּרִבְעָתַיִם.

a17.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדַּאי חָמֵשׁ זִיבוֹת סָפֵק אוֹ חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדַּאי וְחָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת סָפֵק – מְבִיאָה שְׁתֵּי קִינִּין, אַחַת עַל הַוַּדַּאי וְאַחַת עַל הַסָּפֵק, שֶׁל וַדַּאי נֶאֱכֶלֶת וְהַשְּׁאָר עָלֶיהָ חוֹבָה, שֶׁל סָפֵק אֵין נֶאֱכֶלֶת וְאֵין הַשְּׁאָר עָלֶיהָ חוֹבָה.

a18.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: עַל וַדַּאי תֹּאמַר: ״עַל הָאַחֲרוֹנָה״ וְתִפָּטֵר. שֶׁל סָפֵק, אִם יֵשׁ וַדַּאי בֵּינֵיהֶן, תֹּאמַר: ״עַל הַוַּדַּאי״ וְתִפָּטֵר, וְאִם לָאו, תֹּאמַר: ״עַל אֶחָד מֵהֶן״ וְתִפָּטֵר. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: בֵּין עַל הַוַּדַּאי בֵּין עַל הַסָּפֵק, תֹּאמַר: ״עַל אַחַת מֵהֶן״ וְתִפָּטֵר.

a19.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרַב פָּפָּא, אֵימָא לָךְ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי, דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי מְדַמֵּי לְהוֹן לְחַטָּאת, דְּמַאן דְּחַיָּיב חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת עַד דְּמַיְיתֵי כּוּלְּהוֹן וְסוֹף מִכַּפַּר לֵיהּ, הָכָא נָמֵי לָא שְׁנָא.

a20.he: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְדַמֵּי לְהוֹן לִטְבִילוֹת, דְּמַאן דִּמְחַיַּיב חָמֵשׁ טְבִילוֹת, כֵּיוָן דְּטָבֵיל חֲדָא זִימְנָא אִיטְּהַר, הָכָא נָמֵי לָא שְׁנָא.

a21.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְחַטָּאת מְדַמֵּי לְהוֹן, אַמַּאי שֶׁל סָפֵק תֹּאמַר: ״עַל אַחַת מֵהֶן״, וְתִפָּטֵר? אִילּוּ מַאן דִּמְחַיַּיב

b1.he: חָמֵשׁ אֲשָׁמוֹת תְּלוּיִין, כִּי מַיְיתֵי חַד מִי מִיפְּטַר? וְהָתַנְיָא, זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁחֲלוּקִין בְּחַטָּאוֹת – חֲלוּקִין בַּאֲשָׁמוֹת!

b2.he: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לִטְבִילוֹת מְדַמֵּי לְהוֹן, וּבְחוֹשְׁשִׁין לִפְשִׁיעָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי סָבַר: חָיְישִׁינַן לִפְשִׁיעָה, וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: לָא חָיְישִׁינַן לִפְשִׁיעָה.

b4.he: מַתְנִי׳ אַרְבָּעָה מְחוּסְּרֵי כַּפָּרָה, וְאַרְבָּעָה מְבִיאִין עַל הַזָּדוֹן כַּשּׁוֹגֵג.

b5.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן מְחוּסְּרֵי כַּפָּרָה: הַזָּב, וְהַזָּבָה, וְהַיּוֹלֶדֶת, וְהַמְצוֹרָע.

b6.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: גֵּר מְחוּסָּר כַּפָּרָה עַד שֶׁיִּזָּרֵק עָלָיו הַדָּם. נָזִיר – לְיֵינוֹ וְתִגְלַחְתּוֹ וְטוּמְאָתוֹ.

b7.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי שְׁנָא זָב וְזָבָה דְּמָנֵי לְהוֹן בִּתְרֵין – מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲלוּקָהּ טוּמְאָתוֹ, דְּזָב לָא מְטַמֵּא בְּאוֹנֶס וְזָבָה לָא מְטַמְּאָה בִּרְאִיּוֹת בְיָמִים,

b8.he: דְּתַנְיָא: ״מִבְּשָׂרוֹ״ – וְלֹא מֵחֲמַת אוֹנְסוֹ. (וּמִי טָמֵא) [וּמִיטַּמֵּא] בִּרְאִיּוֹת כִּבְיָמִים, דְּתַנְיָא: תָּלָה הַכָּתוּב אֶת הַזָּכָר בִּרְאִיּוֹת וְאֶת הַנְּקֵבָה בְּיָמִים. וְזָבָה מִטַּמְּאָה בְּאוֹנֶס, וְלֹא מִטַּמְּאָה בִּרְאִיּוֹת כִּבְיָמִים.

b9.he: מְצוֹרָע וּמְצוֹרַעַת נָמֵי חֲלוּקָה טוּמְאָתָן, דִּמְצוֹרָע טָעוּן פְּרִיעָה וּפְרִימָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״בְּגָדָיו יִהְיוּ פְרֻמִים וְרֹאשׁוֹ יִהְיֶה פָרוּעַ״. וְאָסוּר בְּתַשְׁמִישׁ הַמִּטָּה.

b10.he: וּמְצוֹרַעַת אֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה פְּרִיעָה וּפְרִימָה, דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אִישׁ, אִשָּׁה מִנַּיִן? כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וְהַצָּרוּעַ״ – הֲרֵי כָּאן שְׁנַיִם.

b11.he: אִם כֵּן מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִישׁ״? נִתְּקוֹ הַכָּתוּב מֵעִנְיָן שֶׁל מַעְלָה לְעִנְיָן שֶׁל מַטָּה, לוֹמַר: אִישׁ פּוֹרֵעַ וּפוֹרֵם, וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה פּוֹרַעַת וּפוֹרֶמֶת. וּמוּתֶּרֶת בְּתַשְׁמִישׁ הַמִּטָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְיָשַׁב מִחוּץ לְאׇהֳלוֹ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים״ – וְלֹא מִחוּץ לְאׇהֳלָהּ.

b12.he: הִלְכָּךְ נַמְנִינְהוּ בִּתְרֵין! זָב וְזָבָה – עִיקַּר טוּמְאָתָן חֲלוּקָה, מְצוֹרָע וּמְצוֹרַעַת – אֵין עִיקַּר טוּמְאָתָן חֲלוּקָה, הַאי וְהַאי כִּגְרִיס הוּא.

b13.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: גֵּר מְחוּסָּר כּוּ׳. וְתַנָּא קַמָּא, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי גֵּר? כִּי קָתָנֵי – מִדַּעַם דְּמִישְׁ[תְּ]רֵי לְמֵיכַל בְּקָדָשִׁים, גֵּר – כִּי קָא מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן לְאַכְשׁוֹרֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ לְמֵיעַל בְּקָהָל.

b14.he: וְנָזִיר מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי? סוֹף סוֹף נָזִיר נָמֵי כִּי מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן – לְאִישְׁתְּרוֹיֵי לְמִישְׁתֵּי יַיִן דְּחוּלִּין הוּא.

b15.he: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, דְּקָתָנֵי נָזִיר לְמִישְׁרֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ, נִיתְנֵי נָמֵי נָזִיר טָמֵא! כִּי קָא מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן – לְמֵיחַל עֲלֵיהּ נְזִירוּת בְּטָהֳרָה הוּא.

b16.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גֵּר מְעוּכָּב לֶאֱכוֹל בְּקָדָשִׁים עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא קִינּוֹ, הֵבִיא פְּרִידָה אַחַת שַׁחֲרִית – אוֹכֵל בְּקָדָשִׁים לָעֶרֶב. כׇּל הַקִּינִּין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה – אֶחָד חַטָּאת וְאֶחָד עוֹלָה, כָּאן – שְׁתֵּיהֶן עוֹלוֹת.

b17.he: הֵבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מִן הַבְּהֵמָה – יָצָא, עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים – יָצָא, מִנְחָה וּשְׁלָמִים – לֹא יָצָא. לֹא אָמְרוּ קֵן אֶלָּא לְהָקֵל.

b18.he: מַאי שְׁנָא מִנְחָה וּשְׁלָמִים דְּלֹא יָצָא, דִּכְתִיב: ״כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה״, מָה אַתֶּם עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים – אַף גֵּר עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים?

b19.he: אִם כֵּן, חוֹבָתוֹ אַחַת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה לָא תִּיסְגֵּי עֲלֵיהּ בְּגַוֵּויהּ, דְּהָכְתִיב: ״כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה״! אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, יֵשׁ לוֹמַר: לְעוֹף אִיתְרַבִּי, לְעוֹלַת בְּהֵמָה לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?

b20.he: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ מִנְחָה נָמֵי! מַיעֵט קְרָא: ״כֵּן״.

b21.he: וָעוֹף הֵיכָא אִיתְרַבִּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה״ – מָה אַתֶּם עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים, אַף הוּא עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כָּכֶם כַּגֵּר״. מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הָעוֹף? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַה׳״ – אֵיזֶה דָּבָר שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ לַה׳? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר [זוֹ] עוֹלַת הָעוֹף.

messages.text: 8a

Continued from 7b: the mishna taught that a woman who miscarries on the night preceding the eighty-first day is exempt from a second offering according to Beit Shammai and liable according to Beit Hillel, and the two schools debated the point.
Gemara

The verse states: “And when the days of her purification are fulfilled, for a son or for a daughter” (Leviticus 12:6). The entire clause: “For a son or for a daughter,” is superfluous and serves to include the night preceding the eighty-first day, i.e., if she has a miscarriage at that point she is obligated to bring another offering.
messages.lead: In continuation of the discussion of the mishna, it is taught in a baraita that Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

verse.he: וּבִמְלֹאת ׀ יְמֵי טׇהֳרָהּ לְבֵן אוֹ לְבַת תָּבִיא כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן־שְׁנָתוֹ לְעֹלָה וּבֶן־יוֹנָה אוֹ־תֹר לְחַטָּאת אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל־מוֹעֵד אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en: On the completion of her period of purification, for either son or daughter, she shall bring to the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, a lamb in its first year for a burnt offering, and a pigeon or a turtledove for a purgation offering.

notes.he: דיתירא הוא דיכול למימר ובמלאת ימי טהרה תביא כבש אלא להכי כתיב לרבות אור פ"א לקרבן:
notes.en: [The printed text marks: up to here belongs to 7b.] “The verse states: ‘or for a daughter.’” It is superfluous, since it could have said, “And when the days of her purification are fulfilled she shall bring a lamb.” Rather, it was written for this: to include the night of the eighty-first for an offering.

messages.text: Rabbi Hoshaya would regularly study before bar Kappara. He then left him and came to study before Rabbi Ḥiyya. One day Rabbi Hoshaya encountered bar Kappara and raised the following dilemma before him:

notes.he: ר' אושעיא לבר קפרא:
notes.en: Gemara. He left him: Rabbi Hoshaya [left] bar Kappara.

notes.he: רבי אושעיא לבר קפרא:
notes.en: He raised a dilemma before him: Rabbi Hoshaya [asked] bar Kappara.

notes.he: שהיה תלמידו:
notes.en: Would regularly: for he was his student.

notes.he: לבר קפרא ואתא ולמד מר' חייא שהיה גדול מן בר קפרא:
notes.en: He left him: he left bar Kappara, and came and learned from Rabbi Ḥiyya, who was greater than bar Kappara.

notes.he: בר קפרא בר' אושעיא:
notes.en: Encountered him: bar Kappara [encountered] Rabbi Hoshaya.

messages.text: With regard to a man who experiences a gonorrhea-like discharge [zav], who is obligated to bring an offering on the eighth day of his purification for three discharges, if he saw another three sightings, i.e., experienced an additional three discharges, on the night preceding the eighth day, what do Beit Hillel say about this matter? Must the zav bring a separate offering for this impurity as he would if he experienced the discharges on the eighth day?

notes.he: לזיבה ראשונה ולמחר היה ראוי לקרבן:
notes.en: On the night of the eighth: [the eighth] for the first discharge, so that on the next day he would have been fit for an offering.

notes.he: מי מייתי ב' קרבנות אי לא:
notes.en: What do Beit Hillel [say] etc.: does he bring two offerings or not?

notes.he: ר' אושעיא זב שראה ג' ראיות בלילי שמיני בסוף ימי ספרו שביום שמיני צריך להביא קרבן על זבות ראשון ועכשיו שראה בליל שמיני ג' ראיות דמחוייב קרבן אחר הוא מה בית הלל אומרים בדבר זה כו':
notes.en: He raised a dilemma before him: Rabbi Hoshaya [asked]: a zav who saw three sightings on the night of the eighth, at the end of his days of counting. For on the eighth day he must bring an offering for the first discharges; and now that he saw three sightings on the night of the eighth, is he obligated in another offering? What do Beit Hillel say about this matter, etc.

messages.text: Is the reason for the ruling of Beit Hillel that a woman who miscarries on the night preceding the eighty-first day must bring an additional offering due to the derivation from the verse, as it is written: “For a son or for a daughter”? But with regard to a zav who saw three sightings on the night preceding the eighth day, they deem him exempt, as in this case there are no superfluous verses from which one could derive this obligation.

Or perhaps there is no difference between these halakhot, and just as a woman who miscarried on the night preceding the eighty-first day after childbirth must bring another offering, as it is the night preceding the day upon which she can bring her offering, a zav must likewise bring another offering for this impurity.
@Rabbi Oshaya What does the Babylonian, i.e., Rabbi Ḥiyya, who came from Babylonia, say about this matter?

notes.he: רבי חייא עלה מבבל כדאמרי' התם (סוכה דף כ.) בתחלה נשתכחה תורה מישראל עלה הלל הבבלי ויסדה וחזרה ונשתכחה עלו בני הגולה ויסדוה ומאן נינהו יהודה וחזקיה בני רבי חייא:
notes.en: The Babylonian: Rabbi Ḥiyya came up from Babylonia, as we say there (Sukka 20a): At first the Torah was forgotten from Israel; Hillel the Babylonian came up and established it. It was forgotten again; the members of the exile came up and established it. And who are they? Yehuda and Ḥizkiyya, the sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya.

messages.text: Rabbi Hoshaya was silent and did not say anything.

notes.dh: דקא מייתרי קראי או לבת כדאמר
notes.he: לא הדר ליה ר' אושעיא כלום מפני שצער היה לו שקרא לר' חייא רבו עייה בלשון גנאי ובבלאי שר' חייא עלה מבבל ולא רצה לקרותו בשמו:
notes.en: Because the verses are superfluous: “or for a daughter,” as he said. Rabbi Hoshaya did not answer him anything, because he was pained that he called Rabbi Ḥiyya, his teacher, “Iyya,” a derogatory form, and “the Babylonian,” since Rabbi Ḥiyya came up from Babylonia; and he did not want to call him by his name.

messages.text: @Rabbi Oshaya Do we require the statement of Iyya, i.e., Ḥiyya? Let us review the earlier ruling, as the baraita teaches that the verse that states: “For a son or for a daughter” (Leviticus 12:6), serves to include the night of the eighty-first day. This indicates that the halakha applies only in the case of a woman after childbirth.

notes.he: ר' חייא ובלשון גנאי קאמר ליה:
notes.en: Iyya: Rabbi Ḥiyya; he says it to him in a derogatory form.

notes.he: (הדר בעא מיניה ר' אושעיא מבר קפרא):
notes.en: (Rabbi Hoshaya asked bar Kappara again.) [This line stands in parentheses in the printed Rashi.]

notes.he: כמו אמר מר. לעיל הרי הוא אומר כו' ומיבעיא לר' אושעיא טעמייהו דב"ה משום או לבת או משום דסברי לילה אינו מחוסר זמן:
notes.en: Let us return to the earlier ones: like “the Master said.” Above [it was taught]: “The verse states…” And Rabbi Hoshaya was uncertain whether Beit Hillel’s reason is because of “or for a daughter,” or because they hold that night is not lacking time.

notes.he: ר' אושעיא בר קפרא צריכים אנו לדבר עייה שאתה מגנה לפי שהוא יודע להשיב ולא אתה:
notes.en: He said to him: Rabbi Hoshaya [said to] bar Kappara: We need the words of Iyya, whom you disparage, because he knows how to answer and you do not. [Rabbeinu Gershom reads this line as Rabbi Hoshaya’s reply; the Davidson English gives “Do we require the statement of Iyya?” to bar Kappara.]

notes.he: כלומר היינו כגון אמר מר הרי הוא אומר כו':
notes.en: Let us return to the earlier ones: the matters they asked. That is, as in “the Master said”: “The verse states, etc.”

messages.text: Let us say this dilemma is subject to a dispute between tanna’im. With regard to a zav who saw three sightings on the night preceding the eighth day, it is taught in one baraita that he brings an additional offering, and it is taught in another baraita that he does not bring another offering.

What, is it not the case that this is a dispute between tanna’im? As, the tanna of this baraita who taught that he brings an additional offering holds that night is not considered part of a date whose time has not yet arrived, and therefore it is as though the eighth day itself has begun; and the tanna of that baraita who taught that he does not bring another offering holds that night is considered part of a date whose time has not yet arrived, and consequently it is not yet time to sacrifice his first offering of a zav.

notes.dh: והא דתניא אינו מביא קרבן [קסבר] לילה מחוסר זמן
notes.he: וטעמייהו דב"ה משום או לבת:
notes.en: And that which is taught, “he does not bring an offering,” [holds] that night is lacking time: and [according to it] Beit Hillel’s reason is because of “or for a daughter.”

notes.dh: מאי לאו תנאי הוא דהא דתניא מביא קסבר לילה אין מחוסר זמן
notes.he: והיינו טעמא נמי דמפלת לאור פ"א ולא צריך קרא:
notes.en: What, is it not a dispute of tanna’im, as that which is taught “he brings” holds that night is not lacking time? And that is also the reason for a woman who miscarries on the night of the eighty-first, and no verse is needed.

messages.text: These tanna’im both hold that night is considered part of a date whose time has not yet arrived, and therefore a zav who experienced three discharges on the night preceding the eighth day does not bring another offering.

notes.dh: והא דתניא אין מביא דקסבר לילה מחוסר זמן
notes.he: והכא במפלת לאור פ"א היינו טעמא דמחייבי דכתיב או לבת לא דכולי עלמא סברי דלילה מחוסר זמן ואית להו או לבת לרבות אור פ"א והא דתניא מביא בזב בעל שתי ראיות דחזא מעיקרא קודם ספרו וכי הדר וחזא בלילי שמיני שלש כיון דלילה מחוסר זמן מצטרפי הני שלש בהדין תרין קמאי וכטומאה חדא אריכתא דמיא ומייתי קרבן חד:
notes.en: And that which is taught “he does not bring” holds that night is lacking time, and here, with one who miscarries on the night of the eighty-first, the reason they obligate her is that it is written “or for a daughter.” No: everyone holds that night is lacking time, and they have “or for a daughter” to include the night of the eighty-first. And that which is taught “he brings” is about a zav of two sightings, who saw at first, before his counting. And when he saw again three on the night of the eighth, since night is lacking time, these three combine with those first two and it is like one long impurity, and he brings one offering.

messages.text: And the ruling of this baraita, which taught that he brings an additional offering, is stated with regard to a zav who experienced two sightings. Since this zav has completed his purification process, as he is not obligated to bring an offering, these discharges constitute a new instance of ritual impurity.

notes.he: שזיבה ראשונה בת שתי ראיות היתה:
notes.en: A zav with two sightings: his first discharge was one of two sightings.

messages.text: And the ruling of that baraita, which taught that he does not bring another offering, is stated with regard to a zav who had experienced three sightings. This zav must bring an offering, and the time for the offering has not yet arrived on the eighth night. Therefore, he is not obligated to bring another offering.

notes.he: הלכך כיון דלא יצאת שעה הראויה לקרבן כולה חדא זיבה אריכתא היא:
notes.en: Of three: therefore, since the time fit for the offering has not yet come, it is all one long discharge.

notes.dh: והא דתניא אין מביא בזב בעל שלש ראיות
notes.he: הוה מעיקרא דהא איחייב לזה בקרבן והשתא לא איצטריך לאיצטרופי הנך בתראי לקמאי וכיון דבשעת דחזא בתראי מחוסר זמן הוא אינו מביא אלא קרבן אחד:
notes.en: And that which is taught “he does not bring” is about a zav who had three sightings at first, for he was already obligated in an offering, and now these later ones need not combine with the earlier ones; and since at the time he saw the later ones it is lacking time, he brings only one offering.

messages.text: If the ruling of that baraita is stated with regard to a zav who experienced two sightings, what is the purpose of stating this halakha? It is obvious that this is a new instance of ritual impurity.
messages.quote: with regard to a zav who experienced two sightings

notes.he: בזב בעל ב' ראיות מעיקרא פשיטא דמביא דמצטרפין:
notes.en: About a zav who had two sightings at first, it is obvious that he brings, since they combine.

messages.text: This is what the baraita teaches us: It is specifically if this zav saw a discharge on the night preceding the eighth day that he must bring an offering; but if he saw a discharge on the seventh day he is not obligated to bring an offering.

notes.he: דמצטרפין דראה בלילי שמיני דכבר חוץ לימי ספרו הוא והיינו טעמא דמצטרפין דלילה מחוסר זמן:
notes.en: This teaches us “specifically”: that they combine where he saw on the night of the eighth, since he is already outside his days of counting; and the reason they combine is that night is lacking time.

notes.he: אבל חזא ביממא דשביעי בתוך ימי ספרו לא מצטרפין ולא מייתי:
notes.en: But if he saw on the seventh day, within his days of counting, they do not combine and he does not bring.

messages.text: This is because the tanna of this baraita holds: Any sighting of ziva that negates the days of purity, i.e., which causes the zav to have to count seven clean days afresh, does not bring him to the point of being liable to bring another offering.

notes.he: חשבון ימי טהרתו אינה מצטרף להביא לידי קרבן דאמרינן התם (דחיילא) [דחזא] בשביעי אינה סותרת אלא יומה ויוסיף יום אחד כנגדו:
notes.en: As he holds: any sighting that negates [the count of his days of purity] does not combine to bring him to an offering. For we say there that [one who] saw on the seventh negates only that day, and he adds one day in its place.

messages.text: Why did you interpret that which is taught in the baraita, i.e., that he does not bring another offering, as stating a ruling with regard to a zav who experienced three sightings? If that is correct, let the tanna teach this example in the list that appears in a mishna from the next chapter (9a): There are five people who bring one offering for multiple transgressions, i.e., for violating the same transgression several times.
messages.quote: with regard to a zav who had experienced three sightings

notes.he: בפ' שני (לקמן כריתות דף ט.) גבי ה' מביאין קרבן אחד כו' כי היכי דקתני נזיר שנטמא טומאות הרבה:
notes.en: Let him teach it: in the second chapter (below, Keritot 9a), with “five bring one offering etc.,” just as it teaches a nazirite who became impure with many impurities.

notes.he: תימה היכי ליתני בהדייהו והא ס"ל להאי תנא לילה מחוסר זמן וה"ל כולה זיבה אריכתא ומשום האי טעמא אמרינן לקמן נזיר שנטמא טומאות הרבה דלא מיתוקמא כרבי דאמר נזירות טהרה לא חיילא עד יום ח' וכגון שנטמא בליל ח' דאי לילה מחוסר זמן כולה חדא טומאה אריכתא היא. ואומר רבי דלא דמי זב הרואה בליל ח' לנזיר שנטמא בליל ח' דזב שטהר ז' נקיים נטהר מיד ושוב כשראה בליל ח' ה"ל זיבה אחרת אבל נזיר נזירות טהרה לא חיילא עד למחר ולילה הוי מחוסר זמן כולה טומאה אריכתא היא שהרי עדיין לא נטהר מטומאה ראשונה:
notes.en: Let him teach it with “five bring”: This is puzzling: how could he teach it with them? This tanna holds that night is lacking time, so it is all one long discharge. And for this very reason we say below, regarding a nazirite who became impure many times, that it cannot be established according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who says that the naziriteship of purity does not take effect until the eighth day, even in a case where he became impure on the night of the eighth; for if night is lacking time, it is all one long impurity. And my teacher says that a zav who sees on the night of the eighth is not comparable to a nazirite who became impure on the night of the eighth. A zav who has counted seven clean days becomes pure immediately, so when he saw again on the night of the eighth, it is another discharge. But for a nazirite, the naziriteship of purity does not take effect until the next day, and night is lacking time, so it is all one long impurity, since he has not yet become pure of the first impurity.

notes.he: וליתנייה להא גבי חמשה מביאין קרבן אחד על עבירות הרבה כלומר האי נמי מביא קרבן אחד על זיבות הרבה:
notes.en: And let him teach this with “five bring one offering for many transgressions”: that is, this one too brings one offering for many discharges.

messages.text: The tanna did not include this case in that list because he could not state this halakha as a definitive ruling.

notes.he: כיון דזמנין דאראיות דלילה נמי מיחייב כגון ראה אחת בליל ח' ושתים ביום המחרת:
notes.en: It is not definitive for him: since sometimes he is liable even for sightings at night, for example, where he saw one on the night of the eighth and two on the following day.

messages.text: If the zav saw one discharge at night and then two on the eighth day, he brings an additional offering for these discharges. By contrast, if he saw two discharges at night and one in the day, he does not bring an additional offering.

notes.he: ליה הא למיתני דהא אמ"ר יוחנן ראה אחת בלילה בליל יום שמיני ושתים בשמיני מביא שני קרבן כיון דרובא חזא בשעה שראוי להביא קרבן:
notes.en: It is not definitive for him to teach this, for Rabbi Yoḥanan said: If he saw one at night, on the night of the eighth day, and two on the eighth, he brings a second offering, since he saw the majority at a time fit to bring an offering.

messages.caption: A zav who sees again on the night of the eighth: the two baraitot as Rabbi Elazar reads them, and Rabbi Yoḥanan’s two cases.

messages.text: Know that if a zav saw one discharge at night and two in the day he brings an additional offering. This is because the first sighting of any zav is considered merely semen, since one who has a single discharge of ziva immerses on that day and is rendered ritually pure at sundown, like one who experiences a seminal emission.

notes.he: דאין לה אלא טומאת ערב בעלמא כדתניא זאת תורת הזב ואשר תצא ממנו שכבת זרע זב בראיה ראשונה הקישו לבעל קרי במס' נדה (דף לה.) ואמרו נמי במגילה (דף ח.) שתים לטומאה וג' אף לקרבן אבל חדא ראייה אין לה אלא טומאת ערב:
notes.en: It is merely semen: it carries only impurity until evening, as it is taught: “This is the law of the zav, and of him from whom semen goes out” — a zav at his first sighting was compared to one who had a seminal emission, in tractate Nidda (35a). And they also said in Megilla (8a): two for impurity, and three for an offering as well; but a single sighting carries only impurity until evening.

notes.he: דמצטרפי אחת בלילה ושתים ביום ומביא דהא ראייה ראשונה של זב אם לא ראה שוב אותה ראייה אחת דינה כשכבת זרע בעלמא וכבעל קרי דאין לה אלא טומאת ערב בלבד:
notes.en: Know: that one at night and two by day combine and he brings. For the first sighting of a zav, if he did not see again, that one sighting has the law of mere semen, like one who had a seminal emission, which carries only impurity until evening.

messages.text: And yet if he sees two other discharges they combine with the first one to establish him as a zav and render him liable to bring an offering. The same applies in this case with regard to the eighth day.

notes.he: ואילו חזא עוד תרתי מצטרפי לקרבן:
notes.en: Yet if he saw two more, they combine for an offering.

messages.text: Are the cases comparable? With regard to the first sighting of a zav, he saw it at a time of potential liability to bring an offering, which is why it combines with the next two discharges.

By contrast, in a case where a zav sees one discharge at night preceding the eighth day, since he saw it when it was not the time of potential liability to bring an offering for the subsequent two sightings, as one who sees three discharges on the night preceding the eighth day does not bring an additional offering, were it not for the fact that Rabbi Yoḥanan teaches us that it combines with the other two discharges I would say it does not combine with them.

notes.he: לא מצי יליף דראייה ראשונה בדין הוא דמצטרפין דחזיא בזמן חיובא כו':
notes.en: Are the cases comparable? One cannot derive it from there, since with the first sighting it is right that they combine, as he saw it at a time of liability, etc.

messages.text: And does Rabbi Yoḥanan actually say that night is considered part of a date whose time has not yet arrived, as indicated by his ruling that if a zav experienced two discharges at night and one in the daytime he does not bring an additional offering?
messages.quote: if he saw two discharges at night and one in the day, he does not bring

notes.he: דקאמר ב' בלילה ואחת ביום כו':
notes.en: And does Rabbi Yoḥanan say etc.: since he said, “two at night and one by day etc.”

messages.text: if a nazirite contracted ritual impurity through contact with a corpse and underwent the purification rites, after which he must bring an offering on the eighth day, and he again became ritually impure on the eighth day itself, he brings a second set of offerings. But if he became ritually impure on the night preceding the eighth day he does not bring an additional set of offerings, because he could not have brought the offering at night.

notes.he: נזיר ביום ח' שראוי לקרבן מביא ב' קרבנות:
notes.en: Became impure: a nazirite, on the eighth day, which is fit for an offering, brings two offerings.

notes.he: ח' אינו מביא דלענין קרבן טומאה אריכתא היא דלילה מחוסר זמן:
notes.en: On the night: of the eighth, he does not bring, since with regard to the offering it is one long impurity, as night is lacking time.

notes.he: נזיר ביום שמיני לטהרתו מביא קרבן אחר בליל שמיני אינו מביא קרבן אחר:
notes.en: But doesn’t Ḥizkiyya say: [If] a nazirite became impure on the eighth day of his purification, he brings another offering; on the night of the eighth, he does not bring another offering.

messages.text: Even if the nazirite became ritually impure on the night preceding the eighth day, he brings a second set of offerings.

notes.he: נטמא בלילה דקסבר לילה לא מחוסר זמן:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says even: if he became impure at night, for he holds that night is not lacking time.

messages.text: This indicates that according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, night is not considered part of a date whose time has not yet arrived.

When Rabbi Yoḥanan says that if a zav experienced two discharges at night and one on the eighth day he does not bring an additional offering, he spoke according to the statement of the one who says that night is considered part of a date whose time has not yet arrived. He himself maintains that even if a zav experienced all three discharges at night he must bring an additional offering.

If he spoke only according to the statement of the one who says that night is considered part of a date whose time has not yet arrived, it is obvious that no new offerings are required. What novelty did Rabbi Yoḥanan intend to express?

It was necessary for him to teach the first case, of a zav who saw one discharge at night and two in the day. Lest you say: Since he saw the one at night when it was not the time of incurring liability to bring an offering, it should not combine with the other two discharges. Rabbi Yoḥanan therefore teaches us that the discharges do combine with each other.

notes.he: כי איצטריך ליה לר' יוחנן למימר אחת בלילה ושתים ביום מביא קרבן וכו' מהו דתימא כו':
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan needed to say: one at night and two by day, he brings an offering, etc.; lest you say, etc.

messages.text: Mishna

With regard to a woman who has in her case uncertainty concerning five births, and likewise a woman with regard to whom there is uncertainty concerning five irregular discharges of blood from the uterus [ziva], she brings one offering, and then she may partake of the meat of offerings. And the remaining offerings are not an obligation for her.

notes.he: מתני' ספק זיבה כגון [טועה] שראתה ג' ימים ואינה יודעת אם בימי נדותה אם בימי זיבה מביאה קרבן ואינו נאכל:
notes.en: Mishna. An uncertain ziva: for example, [a woman who lost count] who saw [blood] for three days and does not know whether it was in her days of menstruation or in her days of ziva. She brings an offering, and it is not eaten.

notes.he: ספק לידה כגון שהפילה ואין ידוע מה:
notes.en: An uncertain birth: for example, she miscarried and it is not known what [it was].

notes.dh: האשה שיש עליה ה' ספקות של לידה או ה' של ספק זיבה מביאה קרבן אחד
notes.he: חטאת העוף הבאה על הספק:
notes.en: A woman who has five uncertain births or five uncertain zivot brings one offering: the bird sin offering that comes for an uncertainty.

notes.he: שהרי הקרבן הזה לטהרה בא והרי הוא כטבילה אם נטמאת האשה כמה טומאות טבילה אחת עולה לכולן אף קרבן זה כן:
notes.en: And she may partake of offerings: since this offering comes for purification, and it is like immersion. If a woman became impure with several impurities, one immersion counts for all of them; this offering is the same.

notes.he: לא הצריכוה חכמים להביאן שאף האחת בקושי התירו להקריבה ספק מליקת חולין למזבח שאם לא כן אין לה תקנה ליטהר בקדשים:
notes.en: And the remaining offerings are not an obligation for her: the Sages did not require her to bring them, since even the one they permitted only with difficulty, [as it means] offering on the altar a bird killed by pinching that is perhaps non-sacred; and [they permitted it] because otherwise she would have no remedy to become pure for sacrificial food.

notes.dh: האשה שיש עליה ספק חמש לידות
notes.he: ספק אם ילדה הוא או ספק ולד:
notes.en: A woman who has an uncertainty of five births: uncertain whether she gave birth, or uncertain whether it was an offspring.

notes.he: ספק אם ראתה שלש זיבות קודם נדתה או בתוך אחד עשר יום שבין נדה לנדה שהיא שומרת יום ולא זבה:
notes.en: Or an uncertainty of five discharges: uncertain whether she saw three discharges before her menstrual period or within the eleven days between one period and the next, when she is one who watches a day [for a day] and not a zava.

notes.he: מספק ומותרת ליכל בזבחים:
notes.en: She brings one offering: out of uncertainty, and she is permitted to eat offerings.

notes.he: דקרבנות האחרים עלה חובה להביא הואיל וספק לידות היו:
notes.en: And the remaining: the other offerings are not an obligation for her to bring, since they were uncertain births.

messages.text: If she experienced five definite discharges of a zava or five definite births, she brings one offering, and then she may partake of the meat of offerings. And the remaining offerings are an obligation for her.

notes.dh: ה' לידות ודאות או ה' זיבות ודאות מביאה קרבן אחד ואוכלת בזבחים
notes.he: כמו שפירשתי:
notes.en: Five definite births or five definite zivot: she brings one offering and partakes of offerings, as I explained.

notes.he: כדאמרינן לקמן בפ' שני (כריתות ד' ט:) יכול תביא על הלידה שלפני מלאת ועל הלידה שלאחר מלאת קרבן אחד לשניהם ת"ל זאת:
notes.en: And the remaining offerings are an obligation for her: as we say below in the second chapter (Keritot 9b): One might think she brings one offering for both a birth before the completion [of her days] and a birth after the completion; the verse states: “This [is the law]” [Leviticus 12:7].

notes.he: אבל אם היו עליה חמש לידות ודאות או חמש זיבות ודאות מביאה קרבן א' ואוכלת בזבחים והשאר עליה חובה להביא:
notes.en: But if she had five definite births or five definite discharges, she brings one offering and eats offerings, and the remaining are an obligation for her to bring.

messages.text: There was an incident where the price of nests, i.e., pairs of birds, stood in Jerusalem at one gold dinar, as the great demand for birds for the offerings of a woman after childbirth and a zava led to an increase in the price.

notes.he: שני קינין ד' תורין:
notes.en: Nests: two nests, four turtledoves.

notes.he: בשני זהובין קן לדינר זהב:
notes.en: At a gold dinar: at two gold coins, a nest for a gold dinar.

notes.he: ומעשה שעמדו קינין של יולדות ושל זבות בירושלים בדינר זהב הקן מפני שאמרו השאר עליה חובה ובאו נשים הרבה שהיו עליהן חמש לידות ודאות וזיבות ודאות ורבו לקנות והוקירו הקינין:
notes.en: There was an incident where nests, of women after childbirth and of zavot, stood in Jerusalem at a gold dinar per nest, because they had said “the remaining are an obligation for her.” Many women who had five definite births and definite discharges came, and many bought, and they made the nests expensive.

messages.text: I swear by this abode of the Divine Presence that I will not lie down tonight until the price of nests will be in silver dinars.

notes.he: שבועה:
notes.en: This abode: an oath.

messages.text: A woman who has in her case five definite discharges of a zava or five definite births brings one offering, and then she may partake of the meat of offerings. And the remaining offerings are not an obligation for her.
messages.lead: Ultimately, he entered the court and taught:

notes.he: אע"פ שהיקל על דברי תורה עת לעשות לה' הוא שאלמלי לא ימצאו יחדלו מלהביא אפילו אחד ויאכלו בקדשים בטומאת הגוף:
notes.en: He entered the court to teach etc.: although he was lenient against the words of the Torah, it was “a time to act for the Lord” [Psalms 119:126]. For if they could not find [birds], they would stop bringing even one, and would eat sacrificial food in bodily impurity.

notes.he: נראה שלא היקל על ד"ת אלא לטבילות מדמי לה לגמרי דאי מחוייב ה' טבילות כיון דטבל ליה חדא אין צריך לטבול עוד:
notes.en: He entered the court and taught: It seems that he was not lenient against the words of the Torah; rather, he compares it entirely to immersions. For if one is obligated in five immersions, once he has immersed one time he need not immerse again.

notes.he: נשבע במי ששיכן שמו בבית הזה שלא אלין הלילה עד שאזלזל הקינין עד שיעמדו בדינרין של כסף ונכנס לב"ד בלשכת הגזית ולימד האשה כו' מביאה קרבן אחד על האחרות שבהן ואוכלת בזבחים ופטורה ואין השאר עליה חובה והוזלו הקינין מפני ההוראה זו ועמדו בו ביום ברבעתיים בחצי דינר של כסף שבלשונם ובלשון הברייתא קורין לחצי דינר ריבוע:
notes.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: This abode. He swore by the One who rested His name in this House: “I will not lie down tonight until I lower [the price of] the nests, until they stand at silver dinars.” And he entered the court in the Chamber of Hewn Stone and taught: A woman, etc., brings one offering for the others among them, and eats offerings and is exempt, and the remaining are not an obligation for her. And the nests became cheap because of this ruling, and that day they stood at rivatayim, at half a silver dinar, for in their language and in the language of the baraita they call half a dinar a ribua. [The Davidson English renders “one-quarter.”]

messages.text: And as a result, the price of the nests stood that day at one-quarter of a silver dinar, as the demand for nests decreased.

notes.he: ב' קינין בשני רביעי דינר כסף. ל"א רבעתים לשון חצי הוא:
notes.en: Nests at rivatayim: two nests for two quarters of a silver dinar. Another version: rivatayim is a term for half.

messages.text: The Hebrew of the mishna here reads בַּסּוֹף, “ultimately,” marked for correction to כֶּסֶף, “silver”; the English above renders both.
Gemara

If a woman has the obligations of five definite births and five uncertain discharges of a zava, or five definite births and five uncertain births, she brings two nests, one for the definite obligation and one for the uncertain obligation.

notes.dh: גמ' ה"ג בתוספתא ה' לידות ודאי וה' לידות ספק כו' ר' יוחנן בן נורי אומר על הודאי
notes.he: חיישינן לפשיעה דאי אמרת תביא על אחת מהן שמא יש אשה שתלד לידה אחת ודאית ואינה רוצה להביא קרבן שתאמר והלא אשתקד היו עלי ה' לידות ודאות ולא הבאתי קרבן על ד' מהן ועכשיו אני מביאה ור"ע סבר כיון דלא אכלה אשתקד בלא שום קרבן לא פשעה:
notes.en: Gemara. This is our reading in the Tosefta: “five definite births and five uncertain births etc.” [The printed Gemara also has “five definite births and five uncertain discharges.”] Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says: For the definite: we are concerned for negligence. For if you say she brings it for one of them, perhaps there is a woman who will give birth once, definitely, and will not want to bring an offering, and will say: “Last year I had five definite births and I did not bring an offering for four of them, and now I am to bring one?” And Rabbi Akiva holds: since last year she did not eat without any offering at all, she will not be negligent.

notes.dh: חמש לידות ודאות וחמש לידות ספק
notes.he: כך כתוב בתוספתא וכך מיסתבר יותר:
notes.en: Five definite births and five uncertain births: so it is written in the Tosefta, and this is more reasonable.

notes.he: מביאה ב' קינין אחת על הודאי כו' ולא יותר:
notes.en: She brings two nests, one for the definite, etc., and no more.

messages.text: That which she brought for the definite obligation is eaten by the priests, and the remaining offerings are an obligation for her. That which she brought for the uncertain obligation is not eaten, and the remaining offerings are not an obligation for her.

notes.he: אני מביאה ותפטר על השאר. ר"ע אומר תאמר על אחת מהן ואינה צריכה לומר על האחרונה ותפטר על השאר:
notes.en: She should say: For the last: “I am bringing it,” and she is exempt from the rest. Rabbi Akiva says: She should say “for one of them,” and need not say “for the last,” and she is exempt from the rest.

messages.text: With regard to offerings brought for the definite obligation, she should say: I am bringing the offering for the last definite obligation, and she is exempt from bringing the rest of the offerings. The reason is so that she should not think that no atonement is required for the others.

notes.dh: ועל הודאי תאמר על האחרונה ותפטר
notes.he: עכשיו מחיוב שאר קרבנות ואוכלת בזבחים היום ולמחר תקריב שאר קרבנות:
notes.en: And for the definite she should say “for the last” and she is exempt: now, from the obligation of the remaining offerings, and she partakes of offerings today, and tomorrow she will offer the remaining offerings.

messages.text: With regard to offerings brought for the uncertain obligation, if there is a definite obligation among the uncertain offerings she should say: I am bringing it for the definite obligation, and she is exempt from the rest. But if there is no definite obligation she should say: I am bringing the offering for any one of them, not necessarily for the last one, and she is exempt.

notes.he: ממין הספק דאמר על הודאי כדי שתיעשה ודאי ותהא נאכלת ותפטר לגמרי כדפרישית במתני' דבקושי התירו להקריב ספק:
notes.en: If there is a definite one among them: of the same kind as the uncertainty, she says “for the definite,” so that it becomes a definite [offering] and is eaten, and she is entirely exempt; as I explained in the mishna, that they permitted offering an uncertain [bird] only with difficulty.

notes.he: ואפילו על הראשונה:
notes.en: For one of them: even for the first.

notes.dh: ור' יוחנן בן נורי אומר על הודאי תאמר
notes.he: בפירוש על האחרונה אני מביאה ותיפטר מן האחרים ועל אותן של ספק אם יש לידה או זיבה אחת ודאי בינייהו תאמר על הודאי אני מביאה ותיפטר על השאר:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says: For the definite she should say explicitly, “I am bringing it for the last,” and she is exempt from the others. And for those that are uncertain, if there is one definite birth or discharge among them, she says, “I am bringing it for the definite,” and is exempt from the rest.

messages.text: Whether she brings her offering for the definite obligation or whether she brings it for the uncertain obligation, she should say: I am bringing it for one of them, and she is exempt.

notes.he: אינה צריכה לומר על האחרונה אני מביאה: בדר"ע ל"ג ותפטר:
notes.en: Whether for the definite etc.: she need not say “I am bringing it for the last.” In Rabbi Akiva’s statement we do not read “and she is exempt.” [The Davidson English, following the printed text, includes it.]

messages.text: @Rav Pappa I will say a statement to you in the name of Rava: With regard to these tanna’im, with regard to what matter do they disagree?

Their disagreement is that Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, who requires her to bring the offering for her definite obligation for the last definite obligation, compares the offerings of a woman after childbirth to a sin offering brought for a transgression. As, one who is liable to bring five sin offerings does not achieve atonement until he brings all of them, and only the offering that he brings at the end atones for him. Here too, it is no different, and therefore she achieves atonement and may consume sacrificial food only if she brings an offering for her last obligation.

notes.he: לא מכפרת אם הביא חטאת ראשונה עדיין חטאים האחרים עומדין אף כאן אם הביאה על הראשונות עדיין טומאה האחרונה במקומה ולא טהרה לאכול בקדשים לפיכך תאמר על האחרונה וטהרה והראשונות תביא לאחר זמן:
notes.en: Until he brings all of them: it does not atone. If he brought the first sin offering, the other sins still stand. Here too, if she brought for the earlier ones, the last impurity is still in its place, and she is not purified to eat sacrificial food. Therefore she says “for the last,” and is purified, and she brings for the earlier ones later.

notes.dh: רבי יוחנן בן נורי מדמי ליה לחטאת
notes.he: תימה א"כ מאי חילק בין ראשונה לאחרונה ואדרבה תצטרך להביא כולן ולא תיסגי לה בקן א':
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri compares it to a sin offering: This is puzzling: if so, what difference is there between the first and the last? On the contrary, she should need to bring all of them, and one nest should not suffice for her.

notes.he: דר' יוחנן בן נורי דאמר על האחרונה מדמי להון לחטאת דמאן דמיחייב חמש חטאות עד דמייתי כולהון וסוף כי השלים האחרונה נכפר ליה הכא נמי לא שנא דמביא על האחרונה ודמי כולהו כטומאה אריכתא וכמביא קרבן אכולהו דמי ומיכפר:
notes.en: For Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, who says “for the last,” compares them to a sin offering: one who is liable for five sin offerings, until he brings all of them; and in the end, when he completes the last, he is atoned. Here too it is no different: she brings for the last, and they are all like one long impurity, and it is as if she brought an offering for all of them, and she is atoned.

messages.text: And Rabbi Akiva compares the offerings of a woman after childbirth to immersions in a ritual bath. As with regard to one who is obligated to perform five immersions, once he has immersed one time he is purified. Here too, it is no different, and consequently as soon as she brings an offering for any of the obligations she is ritually pure and is permitted to partake of sacrificial food.

notes.he: אפי' אמר על הראשונה אני טובל טהר מכל טומאה:
notes.en: One who is obligated in five immersions: even if he said, “I am immersing for the first,” he is purified of every impurity.

notes.he: דקאמר על אחת מהן על איזו שירצה מדמי להון לטבילות דמאן דמיחייב חמש טבילות כיון דטביל חדא זימנא איטהר הכא נמי לא שנא ובהאי קרא קא מיפלגי וכפר עליה הכהן וטהרה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Akiva, who says “for one of them,” whichever she wishes, compares them to immersions: one who is obligated in five immersions, once he has immersed one time he is purified. Here too it is no different. And they disagree about this verse: “And the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be pure” [Leviticus 12:8].

notes.dh: ר' יוחנן בן נורי סבר וטהרה בחטאת קא מיירי הלכך מדמי להון לחטאות
notes.he: ור' עקיבא סבר וטהרה בטבילה קא מיירי הילכך מדמי להון לטבילות:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri holds that “and she shall be pure” speaks of the sin offering; therefore he compares them to sin offerings. And Rabbi Akiva holds that “and she shall be pure” speaks of immersion; therefore he compares them to immersions.

messages.text: @Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak If it enters your mind that Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri compares the offerings of a woman after childbirth to a sin offering, why then, with regard to offerings brought for the uncertain obligation, should she say: I am bringing it for any one of them, and she is exempt? If one who is obligated
messages.quote: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri … compares the offerings of a woman after childbirth to a sin offering

messages.text: 8b
to bring five provisional guilt offerings, when he brings one offering is he exempt from bringing the rest?

notes.dh: אילו מאן דמחייב חמש אשמות תלויין
notes.he: להכי מדמו להו לאשמות תלויין דאשמות תלויין הוו ספק כי הני וחלוקין באשמות בעי איתויי אשם תלוי אכל חד וחד הכא נמי בעי אייתויי אכל ספק לידה ולידה:
notes.en: [The printed text marks: up to here belongs to 8a.] “If one who is obligated in five provisional guilt offerings”: they are compared to provisional guilt offerings because provisional guilt offerings come for an uncertainty, like these; and since they are divided with regard to guilt offerings, he must bring a provisional guilt offering for each one. Here too she should have to bring for each uncertain birth.

messages.text: this is the principle: In any case where one’s transgressions are divided with regard to sin offerings, i.e., where one must bring a separate sin offering for each act when he becomes aware that he has sinned, they are likewise divided with regard to provisional guilt offerings, when there is uncertainty as to whether or not he sinned?
messages.lead: But isn’t it taught in a baraita that

messages.text: Rather, everyone agrees that we compare the sin offerings of a woman after childbirth and a zava to immersions, and therefore by Torah law it is sufficient for her to say: I am bringing it for one of them. And they disagree with regard to whether we are concerned for her negligence.

Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri maintains we are concerned for her negligence. In other words, if she says: I am bringing it for one of my obligations, if she gives birth in the following years she might think that she does not need to bring an offering for each birth, and she will neglect to bring an offering. By requiring her to declare: I am bringing the offering for the last definite obligation, the Sages thereby remind her that all her births require offerings.

notes.he: אם לא הצריכוה לומר על האחרונה אני מביאה תהא סוברת שנפטרה בקרבן זה ולא יהו השאר עליה חובה ותפשע ולא תביאם וכי מצרכת לה לומר על האחרונה אני מביאה ידעה דהשאר עליה חובה אבל על הספק שאין השאר עליה חובה לא מזקקינן לה לומר על האחרונה אני מביאה:
notes.en: Five provisional guilt offerings [etc.] … We are concerned for negligence: if they did not require her to say “I am bringing it for the last,” she would think that she was exempted by this offering and that the rest are not an obligation for her, and she would be negligent and not bring them. But when she is required to say “I am bringing it for the last,” she knows that the rest are an obligation for her. But for the uncertain, where the rest are not an obligation for her, we do not trouble her to say “I am bringing it for the last.”

notes.dh: אלא דכולי עלמא לטבילות מדמי להון ובחוששין לפשיעה קא מיפלגי דר' יוחנן בן נורי
notes.he: דאמר תאמר על האחרות ותיפטר משום דסבר חוששין לפשיעה דאי אמרת תאמר על אחת מהן ותיפטר שמא יש אשה שתלד לידה אחת ודאית ואינה רוצה להביא קרבן שתאמר והלא אישתקד היו עלי חמש לידות ודאות ולא הבאתי קרבן על ארבע מהן ועכשיו נמי אינה מביאה קרבן על לידה זו ופשעה ואינה מביאה אבל כשנאמר תאמר על האחרונה סברה זה שחייבוני לומר על האחרונה היינו טעם דשם לידה אחת היא והוי משמע כאילו אחרונה כיפרה על כולם אף עכשיו איני נפטרת בלא קרבן:
notes.en: Rather, everyone compares them to immersions, and they disagree about whether we are concerned for negligence. Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, who says she should say “for the last” and be exempt, does so because he holds that we are concerned for negligence. For if you say she should say “for one of them” and be exempt, perhaps there is a woman who will give birth once, definitely, and will not want to bring an offering, saying: “Last year I had five definite births and I did not bring an offering for four of them”; and now too she does not bring an offering for this birth, and she is negligent and does not bring it. But when we say she should say “for the last,” she thinks: the reason they obliged me to say “for the last” is that it is all under the name of one birth, and it implies that the last atoned for all of them; so now too I am not exempt without an offering.

messages.text: And Rabbi Akiva maintains we are not concerned for her negligence, and therefore it is sufficient for her to say: I am bringing the offering for one of them.

notes.he: ואני שמעתי חוששין לפשיעה שמא תפשע ולא תביא אפילו קרבן אחד ותאכל זבחים בטומאת הגוף וקשיא לי בגוה טובא חדא אפשר היא מתיא קרבנה ומשום דלא מצרכת לה לומר על האחרונה ליחוש שמא תחזור בה ועוד אי חיישת להכי כל שכן דעל הספק היא מקילה ואמאי לא מצרכת לה לומר על האחרונה ליחוש שמא תחזור בה ולא תביאנו ואכלה בקדשים בספק טומאת הגוף:
notes.en: And Rabbi Akiva is not concerned for negligence: And I heard [another explanation]: “we are concerned for negligence,” lest she be negligent and not bring even one offering, and eat sacrificial food in bodily impurity. And it is very difficult for me. First: is it possible that she brings her offering, and yet, because she is not required to say “for the last,” we should be concerned that she will retract? And further: if you are concerned for that, all the more so with the uncertain she is lenient; so why is she not required to say “for the last,” lest she retract and not bring it, and eat sacrificial food in uncertain bodily impurity?

notes.he: דאמר על אחת מהן סבר לפשיעה לא חיישינן דכיון דידעה דלא נפטרה אישתקד בלא שום קרבן אף השתא נמי אינה נפטרת ותביא קרבן:
notes.en: And Rabbi Akiva, who says “for one of them,” holds that we are not concerned for negligence: since she knows that last year she was not exempted without any offering, now too she is not exempt, and she will bring an offering.

notes.he: סליק פרקא
notes.en: The chapter is concluded.

messages.text: הדרן עלך שלשים ושש · Hadran alakh Sheloshim VeShesh: we will return to you, chapter 1, “Thirty-Six.”

Chapter 2 · ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה · Arba’a Meḥusarei Kappara: those who lack atonement until their offering is brought, and those who bring an offering for an intentional transgression as for an unwitting one.
Mishna

There are four individuals whose halakhic status is defined as: Lacking atonement [khappara], which means they had been in a state of ritual impurity and underwent rituals to purify themselves, but since they have not yet brought the requisite atonement offering to complete the purification process, they may not partake of sacrificial meat.

notes.he: מביאין חטאת ולא על חטא אלא לאכול בקדשים:
notes.en: Mishna. Four lacking atonement: they bring a sin offering, not for a sin, but in order to eat sacrificial food.

notes.he: אינן רשאין לוכל בקדשים עד שיביאו כפרתן אע"ג דנטהרו:
notes.en: Four who lack atonement: they may not eat sacrificial food until they bring their atonement, even though they have become pure.

messages.text: And there are also four individuals who bring an offering for an intentional transgression in the same manner as they do for an unwitting transgression.

And these are the four individuals who lack atonement: The man who experiences a gonorrhea-like discharge [zav], the woman who experiences a discharge of uterine blood after her menstrual period [zava], the woman after childbirth, and the leper. In all four of these cases, although the individual has completed all of the other steps of the purification process, the process is not complete until the atonement offering has been brought.
A convert also lacks atonement, even after he has been circumcised and has immersed in a ritual bath, until the priest sprinkles the blood of his offering on the altar on his behalf.

notes.he: דבעי איתויי קרבן כדמפרש לקמיה:
notes.en: Until the blood is sprinkled for him: for he must bring an offering, as is explained below.

notes.dh: ר' אליעזר בן יעקב אומר גר
notes.he: אע"פ שמל וטבל מחוסר כפורים הוא ואסור לוכל בקדשים עד שיביא קינו ויזרק עליו הדם:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: A convert, even though he has been circumcised and has immersed, lacks atonement, and is forbidden to eat sacrificial food until he brings his nest and the blood is sprinkled for him.

messages.text: A nazirite also lacks atonement with regard to his permission for drinking wine, and cutting his hair, and his exposure to ritual impurity imparted by a corpse, until his offerings are sacrificed.

notes.he: ונזיר מחוסר כפרה שכל זמן שלא כיפר אסור ביין ובתגלחת ולטמא למתים:
notes.en: And a nazirite, for his wine, his shaving and his impurity: and a nazirite lacks atonement, for as long as he has not achieved atonement he is forbidden wine, shaving and becoming impure for the dead.

notes.he: ונזיר טהור ששילם נזירותו מותר הוא לוכל בקדשים שטהור הוא אבל מחוסר כפורים הוא ליין שאסור לשתות יין ולגלח וליטמא למתים עד שיביא כפרתו:
notes.en: And a pure nazirite who has completed his naziriteship is permitted to eat sacrificial food, since he is pure; but he lacks atonement with regard to wine, for he is forbidden to drink wine, to shave and to become impure for the dead until he brings his atonement.

messages.text: Gemara
What is different about a zav and a zava, that the tanna decided to count them as two separate cases?
messages.quote: The man who experiences a gonorrhea-like discharge [zav], the woman who experiences a discharge of uterine blood

notes.he: דחשיב זב וזבה בתרין מהנך מחוסרי כפרה:
notes.en: Gemara. That he counts them as two: that he reckons zav and zava as two of those who lack atonement.

messages.text: They are different due to the fact that the impurity of a zav is distinct from that of a zava, as a zav does not become impure if he has a discharge by accident, i.e., due to a cause such as an illness or having consumed certain foods, whereas there is no such exemption in the case of a zava; and a zava, unlike a zav, does not become impure by three sightings of menstrual-type blood on one day like she becomes impure by sightings on three consecutive days.

notes.he: אם ראה זיבה מחמת חולי או מחמת אותן דברים שבודקין בהן את הזב:
notes.en: Becomes impure by accident: if he saw a discharge due to illness, or due to those things for which a zav is examined.

messages.text: The verse states: “When any man has a discharge from his flesh, his discharge is impure” (Leviticus 15:2). The term “from his flesh” teaches that the discharge is impure only if it is due to an internal cause, and not due to his accident.

verse.he: דַּבְּרוּ אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַאֲמַרְתֶּם אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶה זָב מִבְּשָׂרוֹ זוֹבוֹ טָמֵא הוּא׃
verse.en:
Speak to the Israelite people and say to them:
When any man at all has a discharge issuing from his member, he is impure.

notes.he: מכח אברו ומתוקף יצרו:
notes.en: From his flesh: from the force of his organ and the strength of his desire.

notes.he: מעצמו:
notes.en: From his flesh: from himself.

messages.text: And furthermore, a zav becomes impure by three sightings of gonorrhea-like discharge on one day like he becomes impure by three such sightings on three consecutive days, as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: אם ראה ג' ביום אחד:
notes.en: And he becomes impure by sightings: if he saw three in one day.

notes.he: אם ראה ג' ימים רצופין כדמפרש בב"ק בפרק ב' (דף כד.) זבה לא מטמאה אלא בימים:
notes.en: As by days: if he saw on three consecutive days, as is explained in Bava Kamma, chapter two (24a): a zava becomes impure only by days.

notes.he: בג' ראיות:
notes.en: And he becomes impure by sightings: by three sightings.

messages.text: The verse links the impurity of the male, i.e., a zav, to the number of sightings on the same day or on consecutive days, and of the female zava to the number of consecutive days on which she experiences sightings of blood.

notes.he: כזבה בימים דכתיב בזב ג' פעמים זובו:
notes.en: As by days: like a zava by days, since “his discharge” is written three times of the zav.

notes.he: בימים ואשה כי תזוב ימים רבים ימים שנים רבים שלשה:
notes.en: And a zava, by days: “And a woman, if she has a discharge… many days” [Leviticus 15:25]: “days” is two, “many” is three.

messages.text: And by contrast, a zava becomes impure if she has a discharge by accident, and does not become impure by three sightings on one day like she becomes impure by sightings on three consecutive days. Therefore, the mishna counts them as two separate cases.

notes.he: זבה מטמאה באונס כדאמרינן בפרק בנות כותים (נדה דף לו:) וכי יזוב זוב דמה (ויקרא ט״ו:כ״ה) הרי אונס אמור:
notes.en: A zava becomes impure by accident: as we say in the chapter Benot Kutim (Nidda 36b): “And if a woman has a discharge of her blood” [Leviticus 15:25]; here [a discharge by] accident is stated.

notes.he: דלא כתיב בה מבשרה והאי דכתיב ואשה כי תהיה זבה דם יהיה זובה מבשרה האי בנדה קא מיירי והאי בבשרה ילפינן מינה מלמד שמטמא בפנים כבחוץ:
notes.en: And a zava becomes impure by accident: since “from her flesh” is not written of her. And that which is written, “And a woman, if she has a discharge, and her discharge in her flesh is blood” [Leviticus 15:19], speaks of a menstruating woman; and from this “in her flesh” we derive that she becomes impure [by blood] inside as [by blood] outside.

messages.text: But the impurities of a male leper and a female leper are also distinct, as a male leper requires letting his hair grow wild and rending his garments, as it is written: “His garments shall be rent and the hair of his head shall go wild” (Leviticus 13:45), and he is prohibited from engaging in sexual intercourse.

verse.he: וְהַצָּרוּעַ אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ הַנֶּגַע בְּגָדָיו יִהְיוּ פְרֻמִים וְרֹאשׁוֹ יִהְיֶה פָרוּעַ וְעַל־שָׂפָם יַעְטֶה וְטָמֵא ׀ טָמֵא יִקְרָא׃
verse.en: As for the person with a leprous affection: their clothes shall be rent, their head shall be left bare, and their upper lip shall be covered over; and they shall call out, “Impure! Impure!”

messages.text: And by contrast, a female leper does not require letting her hair grow wild and rending her garments, as it is taught in a baraita:

The verse states: “He is a leprous man” (Leviticus 13:44): I have derived only that a man can be a leper; from where do I derive that a woman can also be a leper? When the verse states: “And the leper in whom the mark is” (Leviticus 13:45), without specifying a man, the verse teaches that there are two here, i.e., a man and a woman.

verse.he: אִישׁ־צָרוּעַ הוּא טָמֵא הוּא טַמֵּא יְטַמְּאֶנּוּ הַכֹּהֵן בְּרֹאשׁוֹ נִגְעוֹ׃
verse.en: he is a leprous man; he is impure. The priest shall pronounce him impure; he has the affection on his head.

notes.he: דצרוע משמע בין זכר בין נקבה מטמאין בנגעים:
notes.en: There are two here: for “the leper” implies both male and female becoming impure through leprous marks.

notes.dh: כשהוא אומר והצרוע הרי כאן שנים
notes.he: צרוע דלעיל והאי והצרוע הרי שנים אחד לאיש ואחד לאשה:
notes.en: When it says “and the leper,” there are two here: the “leper” above and this “and the leper” are two, one for a man and one for a woman.

messages.text: If so, why does the verse state: “A leprous man”? The verse removed it from the matter stated earlier, and applied it to the matter stated later: “His garments shall be rent, and the hair of his head shall go wild,” to say that a man who is a leper lets his hair grow wild and rends his garments, but the woman who is a leper does not need to let her hair grow wild and does not rend her garments.

notes.dh: ה"ג א"כ מה ת"ל איש לענין של מטה
notes.he: דלטהרת טומאת נגעים א"א שהרי נאמר והצרוע:
notes.en: This is our reading: “If so, why does the verse state ‘man’? … to the matter below”: for [it cannot come] for the impurity of leprous marks itself, since “and the leper” is stated.

notes.he: דכתיב במקרא העליון לענין מקרא התחתון שפריעה ופרימה כתובה באחרונה לומר לך איש פורע ופורם:
notes.en: “Man”: which is written in the upper verse, [is applied] to the matter of the lower verse, where letting the hair grow wild and rending are written, last, to tell you: a man lets his hair grow wild and rends his garments.

notes.he: א"כ מה צורך לומר איש נתקו הכתוב לדין פריעה ופרימה מענין של מטה מן והצרוע סתם דמשמע [נמי אשה] ונתנו לצרוע של מעלה דכתיב ביה איש פורע ופורם דהיינו דכתיב בלשון זכר בגדיו וראשו. לישנא אחרינא א"כ כיון דמצרוע נפיק בין איש ובין אשה ובין קטן א"כ למה כתיב איש לענין של מטה לומר לך כו':
notes.en: If so, what need is there to say “man”? The verse removed it, for the law of letting the hair grow wild and rending, from the matter below, from the unqualified “and the leper,” which implies [a woman too], and gave it to the leper above, of whom “man” is written: a man lets his hair grow wild and rends his garments. That is why “his garments” and “his head” are written in the masculine. Another version: if so, since from “leper” we derive man, woman and minor alike, why is “man” written? For the matter below, to tell you, etc.

messages.text: And a female leper is permitted to engage in sexual intercourse, as it is stated: “And he shall dwell outside his tent for seven days” (Leviticus 14:8), and not: Outside her tent.

verse.he: וְכִבֶּס הַמִּטַּהֵר אֶת־בְּגָדָיו וְגִלַּח אֶת־כׇּל־שְׂעָרוֹ וְרָחַץ בַּמַּיִם וְטָהֵר וְאַחַר יָבוֹא אֶל־הַמַּחֲנֶה וְיָשַׁב מִחוּץ לְאׇהֳלוֹ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים׃
verse.en: The one to be purified shall wash their clothes, shave off all their hair, and bathe in water—and then they shall be pure. After that, the person may enter camp but must remain outside their tent seven days.

notes.he: שאם היא מצורעת ובעלה אינו מצורע מותר לשמש עמה:
notes.en: And not outside her tent: so that if she is a leper and her husband is not a leper, he is permitted to have relations with her.

messages.text: Therefore, let us count the male and female leper as two separate cases, as the mishna does with regard to the zav and zava. Why does the mishna not do so?

With regard to a zav and zava, they are treated as separate cases because the essence of their impurity is distinct, as the impurity of a zav is based on the number of sightings of discharge, whereas the impurity of a zava is based on the number of consecutive days on which she experiences sightings of menstrual-type blood. By contrast, with regard to a male leper and female leper, the essence of their impurity is not distinct, as in both this case of a male leper and that case of a female leper, the impurity is based on a leprous mark which is at least the area of a split bean.

notes.he: זה בראיות ובימים וזו בימים ולא בראיות:
notes.en: The essence of their impurity is distinct: this one by sightings and by days, and that one by days and not by sightings.

notes.he: דזהו שיעור נגע כחצי פול:
notes.en: A split bean: for that is the measure of a leprous mark, half a bean.

notes.he: המ"ל כה"ג חלוקין בזב וזבה שזה באודם וזה בלובן:
notes.en: Both this and that are a split bean: It could have said in the same way that zav and zava are distinct, since this one is with red and that one with white.

notes.he: דזב בראיות וזבה בימים אבל מצורע ומצורעת אין טומאתן חלוקה דאידי ואידי שיעור טומאתן בכגריס הוא:
notes.en: Zav and zava, the essence of their impurity is distinct: for a zav is by sightings and a zava by days. But a male leper and a female leper, their impurity is not distinct, since for both the measure of their impurity is a split bean.

messages.text: And what is the reason that the first tanna does not also teach a convert, i.e., why does the first tanna not include him in the list of individuals lacking atonement?
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches that Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: A convert also lacks atonement until the priest sprinkles the blood of his offering on the altar on his behalf.

messages.text: When the first tanna teaches those individuals who lack atonement, he includes any matter where the atonement offering completes the process of purification and thereby permits the individual to partake of sacrificial meat. But when a convert brings his atonement offering, it is to qualify him to enter the congregation of Israel through marriage, not to permit him to partake of sacrificial meat.

notes.he: ור' אליעזר סבר גר מייתי קרבן בין לאכשוריה למיעל בקהל ובין לאכשוריה למיכל בקדשים כדאמרינן לקמן בברייתא גר מעוכב לוכל בקדשים וההוא סתמא ר' אליעזר היא:
notes.en: And Rabbi Eliezer holds that a convert brings an offering both to qualify him to enter the congregation and to qualify him to eat sacrificial food, as we say below in the baraita, “A convert is precluded from eating sacrificial food”; and that unattributed [baraita] is Rabbi Eliezer.

messages.text: And what is the reason that the first tanna also does not teach that a nazirite lacks atonement? Ultimately, as well, when a nazirite brings his offering, it is to permit him to drink non-sacred wine, not to permit him to partake of sacrificial meat.

notes.he: מ"ט לא תני הא לאישתרויי הוא: ומשני ההוא לאו לאשתרויי בקדשים אלא ביין דחולין הוא וכי קחשיב כפרה דמעכבא שום אכילה דקדשים:
notes.en: Ultimately, a nazirite: what is the reason he does not teach it? It is to permit him! And it answers: that is not to permit him sacrificial food but non-sacred wine, and when he reckons atonement, it is atonement that holds back some eating of sacrificial food.

notes.he: ונזיר נמי מכדי כיון דצריך קרבן למישרייה ביין אע"ג דחולין אפי' הכי תנייה במתניתין:
notes.en: And the nazirite too: now, since he needs an offering to permit him wine, even though it is non-sacred, even so he teaches it in our mishna.

messages.text: And according to the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov, who teaches a nazirite in the mishna’s list of those who lack atonement, because the nazirite brings his offering in order to permit himself to drink wine, let him also teach, i.e., include in the list, a ritually impure nazirite.

A ritually pure nazirite brings an offering in order to render an action permitted, and therefore Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov considers him lacking atonement. By contrast, when a ritually impure nazirite brings his offering, it is not to render an action permitted, but rather to effect upon himself a new period of naziriteship in purity.

notes.he: ולר' אליעזר דקתני נזיר אע"ג דלא צריך למישריה בקדשים אלא בחולין ניתני נמי נזיר טמא דצריך קרבן למישרייה ביין קסבר ר' אליעזר נזיר טמא כי מייתי קרבן לאו למישרייה ביין קא מייתי ליה אלא שיהא ראוי למיחל עליה נזירות דטהרה כדכתיב והימים הראשונים יפלו ואסור ביין עד שיגמור נזירות דטהרה הלכך לא תני נזיר טמא:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Eliezer, who teaches a nazirite even though he does not need to be permitted sacrificial food but only non-sacred [wine], let him also teach an impure nazirite, who needs an offering to permit him wine. Rabbi Eliezer holds that when an impure nazirite brings an offering, he does not bring it to permit him wine, but so that he will be fit for a naziriteship of purity to take effect upon him, as it is written, “But the former days shall be void” [Numbers 6:12]; and he is forbidden wine until he completes the naziriteship of purity. Therefore he does not teach an impure nazirite.

messages.caption: Who lacks atonement: the mishna’s four, Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov’s additions, and what each offering does according to the Gemara.

messages.text: A convert is precluded from partaking of sacrificial meat until he brings his bird nest, i.e., his offering of a pair of birds, either pigeons or doves. If he brought one young bird [perida] in the morning, he may partake of sacrificial meat in the evening, and may bring the second bird at a later time.
messages.lead: § With regard to the atonement offering of a convert, the Sages taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דאפילו לרבנן סבירא להו כר"א בן יעקב דאמר לאישתרויי הוא דמייתי והא דלא תני ליה משום דלא מיקרי מחוסר כפרה:
notes.en: A convert is precluded from partaking of sacrificial meat: for even the Rabbis hold like Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov, that he brings it to be permitted; and the reason [the first tanna] does not teach him is that he is not called “lacking atonement.”

notes.he: גוזל אחד שחרית:
notes.en: He brought one young bird: one young pigeon, in the morning.

notes.he: ובלבד שיביא השניה כדאמרינן לקמן להביא פרידה אחת א"א:
notes.en: He may partake of sacrificial meat in the evening: provided that he brings the second, as we say below: to bring [only] one young bird is impossible.

notes.he: שתי פרידין:
notes.en: Until he brings his nest: two young birds.

notes.he: אם הביא אחת שחרית אוכל בקדשים לערב ויכול להביא האחרת אפי' לאחר זמן:
notes.en: If he brought one in the morning, he eats sacrificial food in the evening, and he may bring the other even after some time.

messages.text: Furthermore, with regard to all other cases in the Torah where bird nests are mandated as offerings, one of the birds is brought as a sin offering and the other one as a burnt offering; but here, in the case of the convert, both of them are burnt offerings.

notes.he: כדאמרן לקמן בגמ' (כריתות ט.) מדור המדבר:
notes.en: Here both of them are burnt offerings: as we say below in the Gemara (Keritot 9a), from the generation of the wilderness.

messages.text: If, instead of birds, the convert brought a burnt offering from an animal as his obligatory offering, he has fulfilled his obligation, and if he brought a burnt offering and a peace offering, he has also fulfilled his obligation; but if he brought a meal offering and a peace offering, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

notes.he: עולה אחת יצא:
notes.en: He brought his obligation from an animal: one burnt offering; he has fulfilled it.

notes.he: לאו דוקא אלא משום דבעי למיתני מנחה ושלמים לא יצא:
notes.en: A burnt offering and a peace offering: not precisely; rather, because he wants to teach “a meal offering and a peace offering, he has not fulfilled.”

notes.he: אפי' בהמה אחת לעולה יצא או שתי בהמות עולה ושלמים יצא:
notes.en: If he brought his obligation from an animal: even one animal, as a burnt offering, he has fulfilled it; or two animals, a burnt offering and a peace offering, he has fulfilled it.

messages.text: This is because a bird nest was stated in the Torah only to be lenient for him. Therefore, if he voluntarily brought an animal, which is more expensive, as a burnt offering, he has fulfilled his obligation.

notes.he: שתי פרידין אלא להקל עליו אבל אם רצה להביא בהמה יביא:
notes.en: And they said a nest, two young birds, only to be lenient with him; but if he wishes to bring an animal, he may bring it.

messages.text: What is different about a meal offering and peace offering, that if the convert brings these he has not fulfilled his obligation? It is as it is written: “And if a stranger dwell with you, or whosoever may be among you, throughout your generations, and will offer an offering made by fire of a pleasing aroma unto the Lord; as you do, so he shall do” (Numbers 15:14).
messages.quote: a meal offering and a peace offering, he has not fulfilled his obligation

verse.he: וְכִי־יָגוּר אִתְּכֶם גֵּר אוֹ אֲשֶׁר־בְּתוֹכְכֶם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם וְעָשָׂה אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ־נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה׃
verse.en: And when, throughout the ages, a stranger who has taken up residence with you, or one who lives among you, would present an offering by fire of pleasing odor to GOD—as you do, so shall it be done by

messages.text: From this verse it is derived: Just as you brought a burnt offering and a peace offering when you entered the covenant on Mount Sinai, as it is stated: “And they sacrificed burnt offerings, and they sacrificed peace offerings” (Exodus 24:5), so too, a convert must bring a burnt offering and a peace offering.

verse.he: וַיִּשְׁלַח אֶת־נַעֲרֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיַּעֲלוּ עֹלֹת וַיִּזְבְּחוּ זְבָחִים שְׁלָמִים לַיהֹוָה פָּרִים׃
verse.en: He designated some assistants among the Israelites, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed bulls as offerings of well-being to GOD.

notes.he: דכתיב (שמות כ״ד:ה׳) וישלח את נערי בני ישראל וגומר:
notes.en: Just as you, a burnt offering and a peace offering: as it is written: “And he sent the young men of the children of Israel,” etc. [Exodus 24:5].

notes.he: כשנכנסתם לברית ולמצות עולה ושלמים כדכתיב וישלח את נערי בני ישראל וגו':
notes.en: Just as you: when you entered the covenant and the mitzvot, with a burnt offering and peace offerings, as it is written, “And he sent the young men of the children of Israel,” etc. [Exodus 24:5].

messages.text: If so, in a case where he brought one offering from an animal for his obligation, that should not be enough for him, as isn’t it written: “As you do, so he shall do,” which teaches that he must bring both a burnt offering and a peace offering? Why, then, does the baraita state that a single burnt offering from an animal is sufficient?

notes.he: עד דמייתי שלמים:
notes.en: It should not be enough for him: until he brings a peace offering.

messages.text: One can say that this is derived from an a fortiori inference: If a bird offering was included as an inexpensive way for a convert to fulfill his obligation, would the Torah not all the more so include a more expensive animal burnt offering?

notes.he: תימה זב וזבה יוכיחו דאית רבו לעוף ולא לבהמה:
notes.en: A bird was included, etc.: This is puzzling: let the zav and zava prove [otherwise], for whom a bird was included and not an animal.

notes.he: לקינין איתרבי משום להקל כדאמרינן לקמן:
notes.en: For a bird: nests were included in order to be lenient, as we say below.

notes.he: אחת לא כל שכן:
notes.en: For an animal burnt offering: one; all the more so.

messages.text: If so, then even a meal offering should fulfill the convert’s obligation.
The verse restricts the acceptable offerings, excluding a meal offering, as it states: “Just as you do, so he shall do,” meaning that he must not do less than that.

notes.he: מיעט קרא כן יעשה והתם לא הוה מנחה:
notes.en: The verse restricted: “so he shall do”; and there, there was no meal offering.

messages.text: And where was a bird offering included as an option?

The verse states: “As you do, so he shall do” (Numbers 15:14): Just as you entered the covenant with a burnt offering and a peace offering, so too, a convert fulfills his obligation with a burnt offering and a peace offering, as it is stated: “As you are, so shall the stranger be” (Numbers 15:15).

verse.he: הַקָּהָל חֻקָּה אַחַת לָכֶם וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם כָּכֶם כַּגֵּר יִהְיֶה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: the rest of the congregation. uncertain. There shall be one law for you and for the resident stranger; it shall be a law for all time throughout the ages. You and the stranger shall be alike before GOD;

messages.text: From where is it derived to include the option of the bird offering instead of an animal? The verse states: “An offering made by fire, of a pleasing aroma unto the Lord” (Numbers 15:14). Which item is an offering that is entirely for the Lord? You must say: This is referring to a bird burnt offering, which is entirely consumed upon the altar.

notes.he: שאין כהן נהנה ממנו דבעולת בהמה איכא עורה לכהנים אבל עולת העוף ליכא מידי:
notes.en: That is entirely for the Lord: from which the priest receives no benefit. For with an animal burnt offering, its hide goes to the priests, but with a bird burnt offering there is nothing.

notes.he: הוי אומר זו עולת העוף דבעולת בהמה עורה לכהנים ואילו בעוף אפי' מוראה ונוצה אסור בהנאה דהא נבלעין במקומן:
notes.en: You must say: this is a bird burnt offering. For with an animal burnt offering its hide goes to the priests, whereas with a bird even its crop and feathers are forbidden for benefit, since they are absorbed in their place.

messages.text: Continues on 9a: the baraita goes on to exclude a meal offering through the word “so” in “so he shall do.”
